_why: ⏱ 2026-09-27 · LEAD RULING SHIELD-R3, row O-BOXES-UNSHIELDED-FROM-SPIKES. THE PER-IP LIMIT ON THE CREDENTIAL
ENDPOINTS, AS CODE. services/edge-shield keeps one GLOBAL cap per class and never reads the client's address
(the ADR no.011 / ADR no.020 posture, held by tooling/ci/assert-glitchtip-no-ip.mjs). The per-IP half lives in
Cloudflare's own rate-limiting rule on the nikatru.com zone instead — the zone's single Free-plan rule, which
until now guarded only GlitchTip's login endpoint and was edited by hand in the dashboard.
This file IS the zone's whole `http_ratelimit` phase: `rules` below is exactly what the phase entrypoint holds.
· APPLIED by .github/workflows/deploy-workers.yml's edge-shield job, after merge, with
`node tooling/ops/edge-ratelimit-rule.mjs --apply` (a PUT of the phase entrypoint, then a re-read that must
equal this file). Never by hand: a dashboard edit is drift, and the next line finds it.
· COMPARED weekly (and on demand) by .github/workflows/ops-watch.yml's edge-shield job, `node tooling/ops/edge-ratelimit-rule.mjs`:
0 the live phase equals this file · 1 it differs (the step names each field) · 2 could not look.
🔴 THE FREE PLAN READS THE PATH AND NOTHING ELSE, AND THAT SHAPES THE RULE. Cloudflare's rate-limiting
availability table (developers.cloudflare.com/waf/rate-limiting-rules, read 2026-09-27): on Free the rule
expression may use `Path` and `Verified Bot` only — no host, no method, no query; the counting characteristic
is the IP (`cf.colo.id` + `ip.src`); the period and the mitigation timeout are 10 s; the action is block; one
rule per zone. So the expression below names PATHS. Both path families are unique to their host on this zone:
`/_allauth/` is GlitchTip's (Box B) and `/auth/v1/` GoTrue's (Box C), and no other nikatru.com host serves
either.
🔴 ⏱ 2026-10-01 · THE MFA PATHS (`/auth/v1/factors/*`) AND `/auth/v1/reauthenticate` ARE IN THE RULE
(SYN-A2 / PB-01, row O-ONE-CLIENT-CAN-EXHAUST-THE-CREDENTIAL-CAP). Until then one client could fill the shield's
ONE global credential bucket (300/min per colo) and every sign-up, OTP, recovery, verify and MFA step in that
colo was refused at the shield, before GoTrue's own per-IP limiter could tell that client from anyone else. The
shield now keeps three credential buckets (services/edge-shield/src/classify.ts); this rule bounds one address
on two of them (auth-signup-recover, auth-factor). It is still ONE rule: the Free plan allows one.
🔴 ⏱ 2026-10-02 · `/auth/v1/token` IS NOT IN THE RULE, AND MUST NOT BE (lead ruling on PR #1147, item 1;
tooling/ci/test/edge-ratelimit-rule.test.mjs holds it). The grant lives in the QUERY, which a Free-plan rule
cannot read, so counting `/token` counts every `grant_type=refresh_token` call too; Cloudflare's block answers
429; and gotrue-dart treats a refresh 4xx as final — it deletes the stored session and emits signedOut (the
failure LEAD RULING SHIELD-R2 keeps the shield's own refresh refusal at 503 for). Our users are mostly in India
on carrier-grade NAT — one public address for many phones — so a per-IP limit on `/token` would sign out real
users who merely share an address, and would let an attacker sign out everyone behind a shared address by
sending 5 junk password posts in 10 s. The cost of leaving it out: the shield's `auth-password` bucket has no
per-IP bound at the edge, so one client can still fill it (password sign-in refused in that colo for the
bucket's minute) — but it no longer touches sign-up, recovery or MFA, which have their own buckets.
GOTRUE_RATE_LIMIT_HEADER on Box C (ADR no.059 R4-08) gives GoTrue's own per-IP /token limiter the real
address; a plan whose rule reads the query (Pro: Query and Host — a spend, owner-gated) could count the
password grant alone.
⚠️ THE RESIDUAL, with the rule in place: a shared GLOBAL bucket the rule covers is still lockable by about its
cap ÷ this rule's per-IP rate — 300/min ÷ 30/min = 10 addresses at the limit, per colo, for auth-signup-recover
and auth-factor; one address no longer locks either. auth-password is NOT covered (above): one address can fill
it. services/edge-shield/test/wrangler-config.test.ts holds the two covered caps at that ratio or above.
The threshold and the action are the ones the zone's rule already had (5 requests per 10 s per IP, block for
10 s; the owner-proven GlitchTip login limit). The test clients' peak on these paths, counted from code, is at
most 3 in any 10 s from one address, 4 if two laptop scripts overlap — counting the password grants, which
the rule no longer counts (the draft-shield report, e2e runner and laptop), so no test reaches 5. No script in this repo
sends a refresh grant (grep, 2026-10-01); an SDK session in a test run refreshes at most once an hour.
⚠️ NOT VERIFIED BEFORE MERGE: that the deploy token (CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN) holds Zone → Zone WAF → Edit on
nikatru.com, which the PUT needs, and that the live phase is the one rule this file describes. Neither is
readable from a lane. A missing scope makes the apply step answer HTTP 403 → exit 2, and the edge-shield
deploy job goes red where it happened; the live rule is left exactly as it was (the PUT is all or nothing).

rules.description: nikatru credential endpoints, per IP (tooling/edge-ratelimit-rule.json; LEAD RULING SHIELD-R3)
rules._expression_why: No `/auth/v1/token` here, ever (lead ruling on PR #1147, item 1): the Free plan cannot read the query, so it would count the refresh grant; gotrue-dart signs a native user out on a refresh 429; and most users are in India behind carrier-grade NAT, so a per-IP limit on /token signs out real users who share an address and lets an attacker sign out everyone behind one. /factors/ and /reauthenticate stay. edge-ratelimit-rule.test.mjs fails if the refresh-grant path appears.
